commit.message:
feat(sim): judge fixture collisions against the fixture's real mesh

The world-AABB fixture laws (c2)/(d2) stay the broad phase; a tagged
model's closed world mesh now gets the last word on every upright move
its box flagged, and may only acquit. A path down a vise's gap - inside
its one box, nowhere near its steel - posts and generates clean, while
a jaw-corner clip, a rapid into a jaw top, a holder over a jaw and a
tool buried in steel still block the post.

Narrow phase (camcraft_sim::fixture_mesh): each band of the stack is an
upright cylinder swept along the tip's chord - a convex Minkowski sum -
tested against facets by GJK, "clear" only on a proven support-plane gap
over FIXTURE_HIT_TOL (+ the arc chord's deviation); a band clear of
every facet is decided wholly inside/outside by ray-crossing winding +
parity with ambiguity rejection. Object-median AABB BVH, pruned by the
same proof. Open, non-finite, collapsed or oversized meshes refuse by
name (MeshError) and keep the box verdict; posed, C-turned, XZ/YZ-arc
moves and lathe tools keep the box verdict. Where nothing is acquitted
the report is the box laws' own, byte for byte.

Refs #339

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' (#381 HolderStack) into issue/339-fixture-mesh

#381 landed: the fixture laws read a HolderStack. The mesh law follows:
steel_stack takes the same HolderStack (shank, the holder's own bands,
the housing on holder.top), and mesh_refined wraps the *_held laws in
posting::fixture_problems and generate::workholding_warnings - so a
modelled holder body is judged against the fixture mesh band by band.

Merge upstream/main (70c261ba) into issue/339-fixture-mesh-v2

Brings in #464 (fixture-law gaps: stack_span upright rapids + ramps),

Conflict resolutions:
- crates/app/src/posting.rs fixture_findings: main (#181/#470) made the

- Sim side (no textual conflict): #464 rewrote laws (c2)/(d2) through

  wraps the new laws unchanged; steel_stack is the same band list as
  stack_span::upper_bands plus the flute. One semantic fix: judge_move

  band above the flute by its part - the mesh now does the same (only
  the flute reads as Rapid). Pinned by sim fixture_mesh
  a_rapid_kept_by_the_mesh_names_its_band_like_law_d2 (fails on the
  old label). Recorded in docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md.

feat(app): route struck links over the setup's fixtures

#339 slice 5. Generation now plans an upright mill's links against
the setup's workholding instead of only reporting them. A link is the
run of straight rapids between two cuts. If the gate's fixture laws,
or the whole-stack law over each move's true z span, find it struck,
it is re-laid as retract, traverse and plunge at
max(own top, highest steel under the traverse + 5 mm). Then it is
judged again by both laws. A stated Z stroke caps the height. Steel
the stroke cannot clear refuses generation, naming the fixture and
the link. Steel standing over a link's own end column leaves the link
as laid: its FixtureHit stands and a path note explains why.

Links that already clear, and documents without fixtures, are left
byte for byte. Keep-down feed links, posed and rotary paths, canned
cycles and thread or probe paths keep the report-only verdict
(docs/decisions/339-fixture-routing.md).

New module: operation/fixture_route.rs. There is one hook in
generate.rs. job.rs carries the fixture names and the Z ceiling.
fixture::named_boxes_for is new. Pinned by app fixture_route (6).

Refs #339

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge origin/issue/339-fixture-mesh-v2 (19221ecc) into issue/339-fixture-routing

Takes the parent's refresh: main through #470 (incl. #464's fixture-law
gaps - (d2) now sweeps the whole upright stack over each rapid's true z
span) and the parent's band naming of mesh-kept rapid hits. Merged
without textual conflicts; the generate.rs hook and posting.rs's
Result-returning fixture_findings compose as is.

With #464 on the base, slice 5's own whole-stack law (stack_hit /
mesh_acquits in operation/fixture_route.rs) was a subset of the gate's
laws the planner already reads: the same per-band z windows and box
predicate, the same one-owner mesh acquittal, plus (d2)'s flute-disc
test. Removed, with LinkSteel::meshes (read only by it); the planner
now judges struck/re-laid links by the gate's laws alone, so the
generate path's behaviour is unchanged. fixture_route's unit pins hand
the planner the real gate laws (bands_vs_fixtures + rapids_vs_fixtures)
in place of `|_| false`. Recorded in docs/decisions/339-fixture-routing.md.

Refs #339
